 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before

Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 11 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 9428 of 2024
 Radha And Others
 Versus
 Sanjay And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Chetan Joshi - Advocate for the appellants.

Shri Sudarshan Pandit, learned counsel for the respon
 Order
1. With the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 7/2/2024 passed in MACC No.10/2023 by the IVth Addl. Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Khargone, District West Neemar whereby a total sum of Rs.13,33,150/- has been awarded to the appellants / claimants by way of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Khargone, District West Neemar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. As per the appellants, on 31/10/2022 Ajay Bavne (the deceased) was standing near the grocery shop of Idris and was talking with him.

At that time respondent No.1 rashly and negligently came with motorcycle bearing registration No. M.P. 46 MW 7024 from Balakvada-Singun side and hit the same to deceased Ajay, as a result of which he suffered grievous injuries.
He was admitted in the hospital, but eventually died during treatment.

4. Thereafter the appellants filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21548 2 MA-9428-2024 Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of his death.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.
Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.13,33,150/-.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded an amount of Rs.11,08,800/- for loss of dependency and after awarding compensation in other heads total compensation of Rs.13,33,150/- was awarded.
He further submits that the claims tribunal has wrongly assessed the income of the deceased.

He submits that deceased Radha vs Sanjay on 11 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/30030275/
1 Ajay was operating hotel in the name and style of Manbhavan Hotel where he was selling Tea,
Samosa and Kachori and was earning Rs.1000/- to Rs.1500/- per day.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove this claim the appellant Radha deposed as AW.1 and has also produced in evidence Exhibit A/18 which is the Food Safety Supervisor Certificate of competence so as to establish that Late Ajay was operating the hotel and earning Rs.1000/- to Rs.1500/- per day.

He submits that there was no reason for the claims tribunal to disbelieve the income of the deceased when A/18 certificate was produced and statement of AW.1 has remained firmed in cross examination also.
As regards the compensation in other heads he submits that even in other heads inadequate compensation has been awarded.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Co. submits that the claims tribunal has correctly disbelieved the claim of the income of the deceased.

He refers to the cross examination of AW.1 Radha particularly para 13 of her cross examination in which she has admitted that she has not brought the certificate of establishment of shop, the certificate from the concerned Panchayat the accounts and documents regarding the name of the hotel or even the photographs of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21548 3 MA-9428-2024 hotel.
Thus he submits that there was a clear admission in the cross examination that she has not brought any material in support of her claim regarding hotel business of Late Ajay.

He thus submits that there is no material at all to believe the income of the deceased and for this reason he submits that the claims tribunal has rightly taken the income of the deceased on notional basis by treating him as unskilled labourer.
As regards the compensation in other heads, he supports the findings of the claims tribunal and submits that adequate compensation has been awarded by the tribunal.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
8.
It is seen from the Exhibit A/18 that the same was issued certifying that Late Ajay has successfully completed training in retail and distribution (Leve 1) and Covid - Food Safety Supervisor.
It is not a certificate showing establishment of any shop or business.
In her statement AW.1 Radha has stated in para 13 that she has not brought documents regarding establishment of hotel.
She has also admitted that they are poor family and earning on daily basis.

From the statement of AW.2 Idrish Khan nothing has come about business of deceased Ajay except one line in para 1 of the statement that on the date of accident the deceased was returning after closing his shop at home.
Thus there is no clear material to establish the income of the deceased Ajay.
In such circumstances, the claims tribunal has correctly disbelieved the claim of the appellants regarding the income of Rs.1000/- to Rs.1500/- per day of the deceased.

However while disbelieving the same the claims tribunal in para 16 of the award has taken the income of the deceased at the relevant time ie., 31/10/2022 at Rs.5500/- per month by treating him unskilled labour.
There is reference material for arriving at such figure.
By referring to guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority it is seen that at the relevant time the income of an unskilled labour was Rs.9325/- per month.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:21548 4 MA-9428-2024
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hans Raj V/s.
Oriental
Insurance
Co. Ltd. passed in SLP (C) No.3511 of 2020 has held that in absence of any material so as to establish the income of the deceased / injured support from guidelines can be taken.
As such in absence of any other reference material in the case the income of the deceased was taken as Rs.9325/- per month.

sentences.text: As regards the compensation in other heads it is seen from the impugned award that the claims tribunal has properly assessed the compensation in other heads and just amount of compensation has been awarded.
Thus only change is with respect to the income of the deceased.

The compensation for loss of dependency after the change in the income would come to Rs.18,79,920/-
and the total compensation would come to Rs.21,04,270/-.
The claims tribunal has already awarded an amount of Rs.13,33,150/-.

Thus the appellants are now entitled for an amount of Rs.7,71,120/-
over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of the application before the claims tribunal.
10. Accordingly the appeal stands disposed off.
11. In view of the disposal of the appeal, all pending I.A's are hereby closed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
